services_note: No published, verifiable price list or itemized menu exists anywhere (no own site, no booking platform). Several directory pages (dogdog.org, thegoodypet.com, clinics.thepets.net via WebSearch summary) show an identical, near-word-for-word 'full-service pet grooming salon... bathing, haircuts, nail trimming, ear cleaning, de-shedding, teeth cleaning, flea and tick, aromatherapy and massage add-ons' description; this was independently verified THIS SESSION to be reused boilerplate copy across unrelated groomers on the same directory network (confirmed by searching for the exact phrase 'Aromatherapy and massage add-ons' + 'Flea and tick prevention', which returned multiple different, unrelated grooming businesses with the identical sentence). Because of that, this specific itemized list was treated as unverified marketing boilerplate and NOT used as fact. A WebSearch summary also surfaced an unverifiable claim of a real customer paying '$65 for a 10lb Shih Tzu' and an 'on-site non-anesthetic dog dentist monthly' detail, sourced from clinics.thepets.net / reviewsonmywebsite.com, both of which returned 401/410 on direct fetch this session and so could not be independently confirmed; these were NOT used on the site or in JSON-LD. The site instead presents only services independently corroborated: teeth brushing (verbatim confirmed via the real Michelle Rubeck Maus review: 'always comes back perfectly groomed with his teeth brushed'), plus the universally-implied core categories for any full-service dog groomer (bath/blow-dry, breed-specific haircut, nail trim, ear cleaning), presented WITHOUT any invented prices and with a 'Call for pricing' pattern (same precedent as output/angels-have-paws-tallahassee).
services_summary: Full-service dog grooming: bath & blow-dry, breed-specific haircut & styling, nail trim & ear care, and teeth brushing (confirmed via real customer review). No published prices; call for a quote.

images.source: Instagram (@nicksgroomingstudio) direct scraping was blocked (empty web_profile_info payload + 403/429 on IG mirrors after 2 retries each, per pipeline rule). Real photos were instead sourced and individually verified from: (1) cdn.cmac.ws gallery keyed to the exact business phone number 954-533-8321, whose storefront photo shows the actual 'Nick's Grooming Studio / PET GROOMING / 954-533-8321' sign, confirming the whole 4-photo set as genuinely this business; (2) giftly.com's gift-card page for this business, whose embedded JS payload explicitly ties one specific Yelp photo (favoritableId 6268667, tagline 'Nick's Grooming Studio') to this listing - the other ~47 Yelp-hosted images on that same page were cross-checked and found to belong to OTHER, unrelated nearby businesses (a chiropractor, a car dealership, an STD-testing ad, a competing mobile groomer, etc.) via their own distinct favoritableId values, and were explicitly discarded as contamination, not used. All 5 kept photos were viewed individually (not chosen by filename) before use: no blur, no distress, no text overlays, no scared animals, no accordion/collapsed content anywhere.

images.not_used: The ~47 other Yelp-hosted images surfaced via giftly.com were verified to belong to other nearby/unrelated businesses (confirmed via distinct favoritableId values in the page's own JS payload) and were excluded entirely, not merely deprioritized. Generic stock photos found on petnetid.com/dogdog.org/onsitepetgrooming.com (filenames like 'local-pet-groomers-13.jpg', reused identically across many unrelated city listings) were also excluded as non-specific stock, not real photos of this business.
images.count_note: 5 real, individually-verified photos used (task target was 6-14). Additional avenues attempted and exhausted this session: Instagram direct + 3 mirror sites (imginn/pixwox/picnob, all blocked), Facebook page and mbasic.facebook.com (login-walled), Yelp/Wheree/com-place.com direct fetch (403), Google Maps place photos (require JS rendering, not present in static fetch), Nextdoor (found photo was of an unrelated cat-grooming question, not this business), archive.org (no snapshots exist for either profile). Per DESIGN.md's explicit guidance ('si quedan menos de 5 buenas, mejor menos secciones con buenas fotos que rellenar con malas'), the build proceeds with these 5 fully-verified photos rather than padding with unverified/contaminated ones.

brand_vibe: Real logo (pulled directly from Facebook via the public graph.facebook.com picture endpoint, no scraping workaround needed) is a crimson red (#bf1e2e sampled via PIL pixel count) and black wordmark 'Nick's Grooming Studio' with a cartoon Boston Terrier puppy wearing a red bow tie, on white. Friendly, warm, neighborhood-pet-groomer feel matching the storefront and real customer photos (bows, ribbons, warm cream interiors). Base kept LIGHT/cream, accent built as a deepened cherry/brick red derived from the real logo red for AA button contrast, distinct from every palette already listed as used in DESIGN.md (coral fairy #c04e62, caramelo, esmeralda, teal acero, violeta dark, rosa dark, gold dark) and from the palettes of the other pet-grooming builds already in this repo (celestespet coral-rose, angels-have-paws amethyst purple, a-labor-of-love pumpkin-orange/teal).
base_template: templates/light/index.html (Amani exemplar, light base) copied and edited in place per pipeline fase 2 instruction; NOT templates/light-v2.

palette.derivation: accent_deep derived (deepened for contrast) from the real Facebook logo's sampled crimson #bf1e2e (PIL getcolors pixel count on the fetched 720x720 profile picture). accent_mid/soft/ghost and bg/bg-2/ink computed to keep the palette internally consistent and AA-legible on cream, per DESIGN.md token structure.

jsonld_type_note: Used @type: LocalBusiness (schema.org has no formally valid dedicated pet-grooming type). No hasOfferCatalog/Offer block included since no verified prices exist (per verdad estricta, omitted rather than filled with invented figures).
